candidate_title: Auto Trader Group plc Annual Report 2025
supporting_context: Co-Driver is an umbrella brand for a range of AI-enabled products... The first three products include Smart Image Management, AI Generated Descriptions and Vehicle Highlights, all of which assist retailers in getting an advert live quickly and accurately... AI Generated Descriptions leverage everything we know about a specific vehicle... [Board Considerations, same report:] The use of large language models ('LLMs') in real-time creates an additional requirement to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the output is credible and of value to our customers and consumers... The Board acknowledged the risks of using an LLM but was confident that appropriate mitigations had been put in place, including extensive testing, quality controls and continual learning.
provisional_destination_ambiguity: The company's own Board-risk language explicitly confirms LLMs are used 'in real-time' with mitigations 'in place' (not merely planned), which is why this is coded live rather than planned despite Co-Driver being introduced with some forward-looking framing ('a range... we plan to launch in the years ahead' refers to FUTURE additional products beyond the first three, which are already live). No retailer-count or advert-count metric was found directly in the approved sources this session (a 10,000+ retailer / 1 million+ advert figure appeared only in unverified search-summary text and was not used as evidence), so provisional_quantified_metric is left blank rather than invented.
reviewer_notes: REVIEW: authored by combining two passages from the same annual report (AUTO-REJ-002's product description and the Board Considerations section's LLM risk-governance language). Meets all four operational criteria: concrete task (AI-generated vehicle descriptions, image sorting/tagging), user group (retailers/customers), deployment stage (live 'in real-time' per the Board's own risk language, not merely planned), explicit GenAI connection (named 'large language models'/'LLM').
